newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: United Nations extends Guatemala mission.
newsitem.headline: United Nations extends Guatemala mission.

text.p: The United Nations will extend its human rights mission in Guatemala by a year and widen its mandate to oversee adherence to the country's recent peace accords, a U.N. spokesman said on Monday.

The United Nations Mission for the Verification of Human Rights in Guatemala (Minugua in Spanish) has agreed to a request by the government and former leftist rebels to extend its mission to the end of March 1998, Carlos Urrutia, a Minugua spokesman, told Reuters.
"The mission will grow now as far as new functions, but there will not be any great budget change, we will do it with the same resources," Urrutia told Reuters in an interview.

The government and the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) rebels signed a historic peace treaty Dec. 29, ending 36 years of civil war in which an estimated 100,000 people died and another 40,000 disappeared.

About 155 unarmed U.N. military observers have been in Guatemala to observe disarmament of the former rebels, but there has to date been no formal U.N. oversight of implementation of the 11 separate peace accords, which range from cutbacks in the powerful army to Indian rights.

In late June the mission will file its first report regarding general peace accord fulfilment, including guerrilla disarmament, army reductions, ceasefire and the strengthening of civil society, Urrutia said.
Since 1994, when the government and guerrillas signed a ground-breaking agreement on human rights, Minugua has monitored reports of abuses and violations in Guatemala.
Minugua has presented twice yearly reports, chronicling a steady improvement in government-observed human rights while criticising continued weaknesses in the justice system.
